items.t: Calls for a pause on plate-reading Flock safety cameras.
items.q: Rhode Island Governor Dan McKee calls for a pause on plate-reading Flock safety cameras as privacy concerns grow.

items.t: Ceremonially signed legislation amending the Uniform Controlled Substances Act to reclassify simple possession of 10 grams or less of certain controlled substances as a misdemeanor rather than a felony.
items.q: ceremonially signed legislation today that amends the Uniform Controlled Substances Act to reclassify simple possession of 10 grams or less of certain controlled substances as a misdemeanor charge, punishable up to two years, rather than a felony

record.t: Signed a law (2024-H 7091A, 2024-S 2382A) repealing the health insurance commissioner's authority to enforce federal acts or court decisions that invalidate or repeal the prohibition of annual and lifetime limits on health insurance.
record.q: which was approved by the General Assembly June 10 and signed by Gov. Dan McKee Monday, repealed the authority of Rhode Island’s health insurance commissioner to enforce any act of Congress or decision of federal court

record.t: Ordered the Washington Bridge shut down over safety concerns.
record.q: The pace of construction work on the critical bridge, which McKee ordered to be shut down over safety concerns in 2023, was a top issue in the race.

record.t: Signed legislation, in a ceremonial signing, amending the Uniform Controlled Substances Act to reclassify simple possession of 10 grams or less of certain controlled substances as a misdemeanor rather than a felony.
record.q: ceremonially signed legislation today that amends the Uniform Controlled Substances Act to reclassify simple possession of 10 grams or less of certain controlled substances as a misdemeanor charge, punishable up to two years, rather than a felony.

record.t: Was sworn in as the 76th Governor of Rhode Island on March 2 in a private ceremony at the State House.
record.q: Governor Dan McKee was sworn in as the 76th Governor of Rhode Island on Tuesday, March 2 in a private ceremony at the State House.

record.t: Became Governor of Rhode Island in 2021 and was re-elected to a full term in 2022.
record.q: He ascended to the Governor’s Office in 2021 and was re-elected to his first full term in office in 2022.

record.t: Served as Mayor of Cumberland for 12 years, leaving office in 2014.
record.q: Following 12 years as Mayor of Cumberland, he left office in 2014 when he was elected Lieutenant Governor.

record.t: Was elected Lieutenant Governor of Rhode Island.
record.q: Elected Lieutenant Governor in 2014, he used the office to stand up for working Rhode Islanders and support small businesses.

On June 12, Governor Dan McKee signed the Fiscal Year 2027 budget, making key investments to help Rhode Islanders with the rising cost of living, shield vulnerable Rhode Islanders from federal cuts, and continue to support projects that support jobs and the economy.

record.t: Signed legislation expanding access to justice for child sex abuse victims.
record.q: Governor Dan McKee was joined by bill sponsors and survivors to sign legislation expanding access to justice for child sex abuse victims.

record.t: Signed an Executive Order directing $28 million in emergency relief for households facing a winter electricity price increase announced by Rhode Island Energy.
record.q: Governor Dan McKee today signed an Executive Order directing $28 million in emergency relief to help protect all households from a double-digit winter price spike announced earlier today by Rhode Island Energy.
